overview: Reckitt is a UK-based, LSE-listed consumer health, hygiene and nutrition group built around 11 global 'Powerbrands' including Durex, Dettol, Lysol, Nurofen, Mucinex, Gaviscon, Strepsils, Harpic, Finish, Vanish and Veet. The core business ('Core Reckitt') is organised around four categories - Self Care, Germ Protection, Household Care and Intimate Wellness - sold across roughly 80 countries, alongside a non-core Mead Johnson Nutrition (infant formula) business under active strategic review, including a possible sale. Reckitt reports in GBP with a December fiscal year end and has been executing a multi-year simplification: divesting Essential Home (completed December 2025) and paying a ~GBP1.6bn special dividend funded by the proceeds.

business_model.summary: Reckitt manufactures and markets branded, mostly over-the-counter consumer health, hygiene and household products, monetised through retail and e-commerce sell-through (transactional, repeat-purchase FMCG rather than subscription-based). Growth strategy centres on the 11 Powerbrands, premiumisation/mix, innovation-led category creation, and geographic expansion (especially Emerging Markets). A 'Fuel for Growth' cost program is reducing the fixed-cost base to fund brand investment and margin expansion.

revenue_streams.note: non-core; H1 2026 LFL growth +2.0% (Q2 +7.2%) after a soft prior-year comparative; FY2026 guidance low-single-digit growth; under strategic review for sale

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C via retail/e-commerce, sold through retailer and distributor B2B relationships; Mead Johnson Nutrition also serves healthcare-professional recommendation channels
business_model.geographic_mix: H1 2026: Emerging Markets the largest and fastest-growing area (+8.5% LFL H1, +9.4% Q2), Europe -3.0% LFL H1 (improving to -1.5% in Q2), North America +0.8% LFL H1 (+2.8% Q2); China delivered 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth as of H1 2026

main_competitors: Abbott Laboratories and Nestle (infant formula, via Mead Johnson)
competitive_position.market_position: Global leader or top-2 player in several niche OTC and hygiene categories (e.g., Nurofen #1 pain relief brand in Europe, Harpic #1 toilet-care brand in South Asia, Finish the #1 recommended dishwasher-detergent brand globally, Durex a global leader in intimate wellness); Mead Johnson is a top-3 global infant-formula player but has lost share amid litigation overhang and competition

moat_factors.description: 11 brands with decades of clinical/medical credibility (Gaviscon, Nurofen, Dettol) support premium pricing and retailer listing priority
Deep retail and healthcare-professional relationships in India, China, LATAM, Africa driving double-digit growth and low-penetration category creation (e.g., dishwasher/stain-remover categories)
New Science & Innovation Centres (Hull, Shanghai) and regulatory/medical claim infrastructure create barriers in OTC/medicated categories
Category-creating innovations (Lysol Laundry Sanitizer, Dettol Activ-Botany) build new consumer habits that are sticky once established

weaknesses: Reliance on a disciplined but still-unfinished transformation (Fuel for Growth, Powerbrand focus) with execution risk
Mead Johnson litigation overhang depresses valuation and complicates a sale/separation
Loss of share on some brands (Mucinex, Durex in China) against the 60% 'holding or gaining share' target (only 45% achieved as of H1 2026)
Smaller scale and less-focused consumer-health pure-play positioning versus dedicated rivals Haleon and Kenvue, which were spun out specifically to compete in this space
Europe underperformance (LFL net revenue down 3.0% in H1 2026) versus Emerging Markets strength

growth_drivers: Powerbrand-led premiumisation and mix improvement (price/mix contributed the majority of H1 2026 LFL growth)
Emerging Markets expansion, especially China (12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth) and India/ASEAN
Category-creation innovation unlocking low-penetration white space (dishwasher tablets, stain removers, plant-based antiseptics, laundry sanitizers)
Fuel for Growth cost program freeing up capacity for brand investment and margin expansion (fixed costs targeted below 19% of net revenue by end-2027)
Digital/GenAI-enabled marketing and R&D efficiency (new Shanghai R&D center, AI-driven content/concept generation)
Potential divestment/separation of Mead Johnson Nutrition, which would complete the simplification into a more focused, higher-growth, higher-margin consumer health and hygiene business
Continued capital returns (buybacks, progressive dividend) supporting EPS growth per share

business.description: Thousands of lawsuits (2,000+ combined with Abbott) allege Mead Johnson's premature-infant formula causes necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC); despite recent defense verdicts (Inman, St. Louis, Collins, Whitfield), the federal MDL has 775+ consolidated cases and outcomes remain binary and unpredictable, with a $60m plaintiff verdict against Mead Johnson still on record and a $495m verdict against Abbott in a related case

business.risk: Customer/retailer concentration and private label competition
business.description: Heavy reliance on large grocery/retail customers for listing and shelf space; store-brand and value alternatives compete in Household Care and Self Care categories, particularly in Europe
Only 45% of Core Reckitt Top CMUs are holding or gaining share versus a 60% target, with gaps concentrated in Mucinex and Durex in China
Global manufacturing and distribution scale creates recall and product-liability exposure across OTC, hygiene and infant-nutrition categories

financial.description: Net debt rose to 2.5x adjusted EBITDA (H1 2026) from 2.1x a year earlier following the GBP1.6bn special dividend paid in February 2026, reducing balance-sheet headroom
GBP reporting currency against substantial USD, EUR and emerging-market currency revenue; FX was a -0.3% to -0.5% drag on H1 2026 actual net revenue growth versus LFL

financial.risk: Rising finance costs and tax rate
financial.description: Adjusted net finance expense guided to GBP320-340m (FY2026) and adjusted effective tax rate guided to ~27%, up from 24.7% in FY2025, both structural headwinds to EPS growth

regulatory.risk: Infant formula marketing and safety regulation
regulatory.description: Mead Johnson Nutrition operates in a heavily regulated category (FDA, international equivalents) where safety, labeling and marketing-practice rules intersect directly with the NEC litigation narrative

Self Care and Germ Protection brands rely on regulatory approval and medical/scientific substantiation of claims (e.g., antiseptic efficacy, pain-relief indications) across many jurisdictions, creating compliance and claims-risk exposure
Any sale of Mead Johnson Nutrition (e.g., to Danone) would require multi-jurisdiction antitrust clearance

macro.description: Oil-linked packaging and raw-material costs scenario-planned at $110/bbl implying a GBP130-150m FY2026 gross impact, since moderated but still a monitored variable

macro.risk: Consumer spending slowdown in developed markets
macro.description: Soft consumer backdrop in Europe and parts of North America has weighed on volumes even as emerging markets outperform
Russia Hygiene business reported a half-year operating loss in H1 2026, reflecting the complexity of operating in sanctioned/contested markets

execution.description: Simultaneous Essential Home divestment, reorganisation into three Area Presidents, Fuel for Growth cost program and Mead Johnson strategic review create integration, stranded-cost and change-management risk
CEO Kris Licht and a refreshed Board (several new non-executive directors added in 2025) are still early in embedding the new operating model and strategy

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global consumer health, hygiene and household categories show structurally positive but modest volume growth (low single digits), supplemented by premiumisation and category-creation in under-penetrated markets (dishwashing, stain removal, plant-based hygiene) in emerging economies
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - largely non-discretionary health/hygiene staples provide resilience, though premium discretionary items (Intimate Wellness, premium OTC) have some sensitivity to consumer spending
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - net debt at 2.5x adjusted EBITDA (H1 2026) following the GBP1.6bn special dividend means higher rates increase adjusted net finance expense (guided GBP320-340m for FY2026)
key_input_costs: Crude oil/petrochemical-derived packaging and raw materials (scenario-planned at $110/bbl implying a GBP130-150m FY2026 gross cost impact, since moderated)
Dairy/commodity inputs for Mead Johnson Nutrition
Currency (GBP reporting vs. significant USD, EUR, EM currency revenue exposure)

recent_developments.event: Danone reported (via La Lettre) to be in talks to acquire Mead Johnson Nutrition; UBS estimates enterprise value of EUR4.7-7.7bn (8-13x 2026 EBITDA); no signed deal confirmed, Reckitt shares volatile on the reports

First federal NEC bellwether trial (Inman case, N.D. Illinois MDL) and a St. Louis state-court case both resulted in defense verdicts for Mead Johnson, removing all outstanding adverse jury verdicts against the company in NEC litigation

H1 2026 results: Group net revenue declined 8.1% (IFRS) to GBP6,411m versus the H1 2025 comparative, driven by the Essential Home divestment; Core Reckitt LFL net revenue grew 2.6% (accelerating to 4.7% in Q2); adjusted diluted EPS fell 9.7% to 152.1p; FY2026 guidance (Core Reckitt +4% to +5% LFL revenue, 24.9%-25.6% AOP margin) reiterated; new GBP500m buyback announced over the next 12 months; interim dividend raised 5%
Completed 25-for-24 share consolidation and paid a ~GBP1.6bn (235p/share) special dividend funded by Essential Home disposal proceeds; new ISIN GB00BSZBP530
Completed divestment of Essential Home business to Advent International, finalising the 2024 strategy update to streamline the portfolio around Core Reckitt and its 11 Powerbrands

FY2025 results: Core Reckitt LFL net revenue growth +5.2% (Group +5.0%), adjusted operating margin +40bps, adjusted diluted EPS +1.1% to 352.8p, GBP2.3bn cash returned to shareholders via buybacks and dividends; fixed costs reduced to 19.4% of net revenue under Fuel for Growth

Kris Licht continued as CEO through the transformation (organisational simplification from three business units to three Area Presidents; new R&D centre in Shanghai; factory expansion in Taicang, China); several new non-executive directors joined the Board

items.notes: Returned to growth in H1 2026 (+2.0%, Q2 +7.2%) after soft prior-year comparatives
Fuel for Growth programme target; ~GBP1.0bn of one-off cash restructuring/transformation costs expected cumulatively, c.GBP350m in 2026
Announced alongside H1 2026 results; follows completion of a prior GBP1.0bn buyback and the GBP1.6bn special dividend paid in February 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Kris Licht said Q2 2026 growth accelerated on a broad, balanced basis across all Areas and Categories, driven by strong Powerbrand performance and recent innovation, and reiterated full-year 2026 expectations. Management flagged oil-price-linked input cost risk (originally scenario-planned at $110/bbl, implying a GBP130-150m gross FY2026 impact) as a manageable, moderating headwind, and said Fuel for Growth is expected to largely offset stranded costs from the Essential Home divestment. Management reiterated an ambition for long-term sustainable EPS growth while acknowledging a 2026 dilution headwind from the Essential Home divestment.

bull_case: Core Reckitt (ex-Mead Johnson) is accelerating, with Q2 2026 LFL net revenue growth of 4.7% and broad-based improvement across all geographic Areas and product Categories
Fuel for Growth cost program is running ahead of plan, creating margin and reinvestment headroom even while absorbing stranded costs from the Essential Home divestment

A clean divestment or resolution of Mead Johnson Nutrition (litigation de-risking via recent defense verdicts, plus reported Danone acquisition interest) could remove a long-standing valuation overhang and unlock a re-rating toward pure-play consumer health/hygiene peers like Haleon

Strong emerging-markets growth engine (China 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth, India, LATAM) with a long runway in under-penetrated categories (only 14% global dishwasher penetration, 1-in-5 households using stain removers)
Shareholder-friendly capital returns continue (progressive dividend +5%, new GBP500m buyback, GBP6.4bn returned since July 2024) signaling management confidence
bear_case: Mead Johnson NEC litigation remains a binary tail risk despite recent defense verdicts; the federal MDL still has 775+ consolidated cases and a single adverse jury verdict (plaintiffs have already won $60m against Mead Johnson and $495m against Abbott in related cases) could reprice the stock sharply and complicate any sale

Adjusted diluted EPS fell 9.7% in H1 2026 and net debt has risen to 2.5x adjusted EBITDA following the GBP1.6bn special dividend, reducing balance-sheet flexibility just as margin guidance depends on a strong, back-loaded H2 recovery
Europe remains in LFL decline (-3.0% in H1 2026) and brand share-gain metrics are behind target (only 45% of Top CMUs holding/gaining share versus a 60% goal, notably Mucinex and Durex in China)

Multi-year transformation (three reorganisations, Essential Home divestment, pending Mead Johnson separation) carries ongoing execution risk and one-off restructuring costs (~GBP1.0bn cumulative under Fuel for Growth)
Rising effective tax rate (~27% guided for FY2026 vs 24.7% in FY2025) and elevated finance expense are structural headwinds to EPS growth independent of operating performance
